transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. First and foremost: because water is on the floor next to your plug sockets, this is an electrical hazard. If you can safely do so from a distance (without touching wet surfaces), turn off the power at your consumer unit (fuse box) to isolate the appliance. Regarding the leak: this usually happens for one of two reasons. Either water is escaping from the door during washing (often due to a dirty or damaged seal, or items blocking the spray arm), or there is an internal leak that has triggered the machine's anti-flood safety switch. 1. Is the water leaking from the side of the door while it washes?
2. Or is there a pool of water underneath the machine, possibly with the drain pump running continuously?

its coming out the bottom of the door while its washing, with loads of bubbles. its still running!! the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor and the socket is on the wall right next to it

Please do not touch the plug, the machine controls, or the water on the floor. If you can safely reach your consumer unit (fuse box) without stepping in water, switch off the circuit for that area immediately to isolate the appliance. Once it is safe and switched off, we need to understand why there are "loads of bubbles". 1. Excess suds: If you used too much detergent, or a type not designed for automatic machines (like hand-wash soap), the machine fills with foam that pushes out past the door seal.
2. A blocked seal: Sometimes items like socks or underwires get trapped in the rubber door seal, preventing it from closing properly and letting soapy water escape. Please check what detergent you are using and how much you put in. Also, look inside the rubber door seal for any trapped items.
we ran out of tablets so my housemate squirted fairy washing up liquid in. tub is full of suds. i cant reach the fuse box without going through the water i think. what do i do

Do not touch the machine or the plug. Do not try to move through the water to reach the fuse box if it puts you at risk of electrocution. Because the water is spreading towards an extension lead and a wall socket, this is a serious electrical hazard. You must call a qualified electrician or appliance engineer immediately to isolate the power safely. They will need to check that your sockets and wiring are safe before anyone can touch the machine again. Regarding the leak: using Fairy washing up liquid causes massive amounts of foam in a washing machine, which pushes soapy water out past the door seal. This is not a mechanical fault with the machine itself; it is caused by the wrong detergent. However, because there is an active electrical hazard on your floor, you cannot safely run any rinse cycles to clear the suds yourself until an engineer has isolated the power and confirmed the area is safe.
